questions.enonce_markdown: (i) Solve, for $x$, in the range $0^\circ\le x\le180^\circ$, the equation $\cos x-\sin2x=0$. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Use the double angle formula $\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x$:

$$\cos x-2\sin x\cos x=0\ \Longrightarrow\ \cos x\,(1-2\sin x)=0.$$

(Do not divide by $\cos x$: that would lose a solution.)

- $\cos x=0$: in $0^\circ\le x\le180^\circ$, $x=90^\circ$.
- $1-2\sin x=0$, so $\sin x=\dfrac12$: $x=30^\circ$ or $x=180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ$.

Check: $x=30^\circ$: $\cos30^\circ-\sin60^\circ=0$ ✓; $x=150^\circ$: $\cos150^\circ-\sin300^\circ=-\frac{\sqrt3}2+\frac{\sqrt3}2=0$ ✓; $x=90^\circ$: $0-\sin180^\circ=0$ ✓.

**$x=30^\circ,\ 90^\circ,\ 150^\circ$.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
(ii)(a) A function $f$, of a real variable $\theta$, is defined by $f(\theta)=2\cos\theta+3\sin\theta$, for $0\le\theta\le2\pi$. Copy and complete the table below. *[3 marks]*

| $\theta$ | 0 | $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ | $\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$ | $\pi$ | $\dfrac{4\pi}{3}$ | $\dfrac{5\pi}{3}$ | $2\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(\theta)$ |  | 4 |  | $-2$ |  |  | 2 |
questions.corrige_markdown:
Evaluate $f(\theta)=2\cos\theta+3\sin\theta$ at each value (calculator in radian mode), using $\sin\frac\pi3=\frac{\sqrt3}2$, $\cos\frac\pi3=\frac12$:

- $\theta=0$: $2(1)+3(0)=2$.
- $\theta=\frac\pi3$: $2\left(\frac12\right)+3\left(\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)=1+2.598=3.598\approx3.6$ (the table prints $4$, which is this value rounded to the nearest whole number).
- $\theta=\frac{2\pi}3$: $2\left(-\frac12\right)+3\left(\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)=-1+2.598=1.598\approx1.6$.
- $\theta=\pi$: $2(-1)+3(0)=-2$ ✓ (as printed).
- $\theta=\frac{4\pi}3$: $2\left(-\frac12\right)+3\left(-\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)=-1-2.598=-3.598\approx-3.6$.
- $\theta=\frac{5\pi}3$: $2\left(\frac12\right)+3\left(-\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)=1-2.598=-1.598\approx-1.6$.
- $\theta=2\pi$: $2(1)+3(0)=2$ ✓ (as printed).

| $\theta$ | 0 | $\frac{\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{2\pi}{3}$ | $\pi$ | $\frac{4\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{5\pi}{3}$ | $2\pi$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $f(\theta)$ | 2 | 3.6 | 1.6 | $-2$ | $-3.6$ | $-1.6$ | 2 |

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(b) Taking 2 cm to represent $\dfrac\pi3$ on the $x$-axis and 2 cm to represent 1 unit on the $y$-axis, draw the graph of $y=f(\theta)$. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Axes.** $x$-axis from $0$ to $2\pi$: the marks $0,\frac\pi3,\frac{2\pi}3,\pi,\frac{4\pi}3,\frac{5\pi}3,2\pi$ are $2$ cm apart, so the axis is $12$ cm long. $y$-axis from $-4$ to $4$: $1$ unit is $2$ cm, so the axis is $16$ cm long.

**Points to plot** (from the table): $(0,2)$, $\left(\frac\pi3,3.6\right)$, $\left(\frac{2\pi}3,1.6\right)$, $(\pi,-2)$, $\left(\frac{4\pi}3,-3.6\right)$, $\left(\frac{5\pi}3,-1.6\right)$, $(2\pi,2)$.

Join them with a **smooth sine-shaped curve** (not with straight segments). The curve rises from $2$ to a maximum of about $3.6$ near $\theta\approx1$ rad (between $\frac\pi3$ and $\frac{2\pi}3$), crosses the $\theta$-axis near $\theta\approx2.55$ rad, falls to a minimum of about $-3.6$ near $\theta\approx4.1$ rad (just below $\frac{4\pi}{3}\approx4.19$), crosses the axis again near $\theta\approx5.7$ rad and returns to $2$ at $\theta=2\pi$.

Extra points that help the shape: $f(1)pprox3.6$, $f(2)pprox1.9$, $f(4)pprox-3.6$, $f(5)pprox-2.3$.

questions.enonce_markdown: (ii)(c) From your graph, state the maximum value of $y=f(\theta)$. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The highest point of the curve is read on the $y$-axis: about $3.6$.

This agrees with the exact value. Write $2\cos\theta+3\sin\theta=R\cos(\theta-\alpha)$ with $R=\sqrt{2^2+3^2}=\sqrt{13}\approx3.61$ and $\tan\alpha=\dfrac32$, so the maximum is $\sqrt{13}$, reached at $\theta=\alpha\approx0.98$ rad.

**Maximum value $\approx3.6$ (exactly $\sqrt{13}\approx3.61$).**
